[[Image:Dandelin.jpg|thumb|right|Germinal Pierre Dandelin]]
'''Germinal Pierre Dandelin''' ({{IPAc-en|'|d|ae|n|d|@|l|@|n}}; {{IPA|fr|ʒɛʁminal pjɛʁ dɑ̃dlɛ̃}}, 12 April 1794 &ndash; 15 February 1847) was a French [[mathematician]], [[soldier]], and [[professor]] of [[engineering]].

==Life==
He was born near [[Paris]] to a [[France|French]] father and [[Belgium|Belgian]] mother, studying first at [[Ghent]] then returning to Paris to study at the [[École Polytechnique]]. He was wounded fighting under [[Napoleon I of France|Napoleon]].  He worked for the Ministry of the Interior under [[Lazare Carnot]]. Later he became a citizen of the [[Netherlands]], a professor of [[mining engineering]] in [[Belgium]], and then a member of the Belgian army.

==Work==
He is the eponym of the [[Dandelin spheres]], of Dandelin's theorem in [[geometry]] (for an account of that theorem, see [[Dandelin spheres]]), and of the [[Dandelin&ndash;Gräffe method|Dandelin&ndash;Gräffe numerical method]] of solution of algebraic equations. He also published on the [[stereographic projection]], [[algebra]], and [[probability theory]].

* [[Florian Cajori]], ''The Dandelin&ndash;Gräffe method'', in ''A history of Mathematics'' (New York, 1938), 364.
